correctness.rationale: For each fixed shift, disjoint translation cycles and two transition edges give the exact first moment. Gabrić Lemma 14 classifies two noninverse good shifts as a one-site periodic mutation. Every maximal good subgroup is counted uniquely using h>=3 background separation or h=2 differing-half normalization. Möbius inversion counts exact maximal subgroups; the remaining inverse pairs are obtained from the first moment. Exhaustive standard-library verification covered all words in 16 q>=3 instances.

value.rationale: The natural inverse question asks how many rotations of a word are near-equal. The complete q>=3 distribution for every n and every multiplicity r distinguishes the exceptional inverse-pair mechanism from periodic one-site mutations, including half-turn corrections; its explicit divisor structure is materially stronger than a single existence/uniqueness count.
